source.title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Does every subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex have vanishing higher homotopy groups, and therefore is every such subcomplex itself aspherical?

evidence.quote: whether a subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex need also have vanishing higher homotopy groups

accepted.question_text: If a group G has cohomological dimension 2, must G admit a two-dimensional Eilenberg-MacLane complex K(G,1)?

evidence.quote: every group G with cdG = 2 has a two-dimensional K (G, 1)-complex

accepted.question_text: For every group G and integer r at least 1, if the free product G * F_r with a free group of rank r has group weight r, must G be trivial? In the case r = 1, this specializes to asking whether weight 1 for G * Z forces G to be trivial.

evidence.quote: the only group with wt(G ∗ Frr ) = r is the trivial group.

accepted.question_text: For a group ring such as QG, does the weak Bass trace conjecture hold, meaning that the Kaplansky trace and the augmentation trace agree on finitely generated projective modules over the group ring?

evidence.quote: equality of the Kaplansky and augmentation traces

accepted.question_text: If X is a finite 3-complex whose cohomological dimension is at most 2, is X homotopy equivalent to a 2-complex?

evidence.quote: finite 3-complex X with cdX ≤ 2 is homotopy equivalent to a 2-complex

accepted.question_text: Does every finitely generated perfect group have a single normal generator?

evidence.quote: a finitely generated perfect group has a single normal generator

accepted.question_text: Let pi be a finitely presentable group. Define the deficiency of a presentation with g generators and r relators as g - r, define the deficiency of pi as the maximum deficiency over presentations of pi, and define the weight of pi as the minimum number of elements whose normal closure is all of pi. If pi has weight 1 and deficiency 1, must its first L2-Betti number beta_1^(2)(pi) be 0?
accepted.context_brief: L2-Betti number for weight-one deficiency-one groups

accepted.question_text: Let pi be a finitely presentable group whose group weight and deficiency are both w, with weight meaning the minimum number of normal generators and deficiency meaning the maximum value of generators minus relators over presentations. Must the first L2-Betti number beta_1^(2)(pi) equal w - 1?

evidence.quote: Hypothesis 1.4 If π is a finitely presentable group of weight w and deficiency w, then β1(2) (π) = w − 1.

accepted.question_text: For groups that arise as w-component n-link groups for n at least 2 and whose group weight equals their deficiency w, do all such groups have cohomological dimension at most 2?
accepted.context_brief: Cohomological dimension of equal weight-deficiency link groups

evidence.quote: whether they all have cohomological dimension at most 2 is a question of long standing.

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is a finite 2-complex with a retract subcomplex V such that the quotient X/V is contractible. Is the first L2-Betti number of pi_1(X) at most the first L2-Betti number of pi_1(V)?
accepted.context_brief: Topological extension of the L2-Betti hypothesis

evidence.quote: Hypothesis 1.5 Suppose that X is a finite 2-complex, with retract a subcomplex V such that X/V is contractible. Then β1(2) (π1 (X )) ≤ β1(2) (π1 (V )) .

accepted.question_text: For a finitely presentable group pi with infinite cyclic abelianization pi/[pi,pi] isomorphic to Z and with exactly one end, does the conclusion beta_1^(2)(pi) = 0 still follow without assuming that pi has deficiency 1?

evidence.quote: Can the condition “deficiency = 1” in Hypothesis 1.3 be replaced by “π/π  ∼ = Z and πhas one end”?

accepted.question_text: For presentations of groups with weight 1 and deficiency 1, can the asphericity argument based on an injective block in the Fox-Jacobian matrix be extended beyond the semidirect-product case to other such groups?

evidence.quote: Can we extend this argument to other groups of deficiency and weight 1?

accepted.question_text: Can a nonaspherical subaspherical 2-complex, meaning a 2-complex that is a subcomplex of an aspherical 2-complex but is not itself aspherical, have a regular acyclic covering space whose fundamental group is finitely generated?

evidence.quote: Can a regular acyclic cover (of a nonaspherical subaspherical complex) have finitely generated fundamental group?

accepted.question_text: Let S_N be an acyclic regular cover of a finitely dominated 2-complex S with G = pi_1(S), and suppose G contains an amenable normal subgroup E. Can the asphericity criterion still hold without requiring that E not lie in N, for example when N is elementary amenable?
accepted.context_brief: Acyclic cover criterion with amenable subgroups

evidence.quote: can one omit the condition that E not lie in N

accepted.question_text: Is the knot-like case of the Whitehead Conjecture, namely the case equivalent to finitely presentable groups of weight 1 and deficiency 1 having rational cohomological dimension at most 2, equivalent to the finite Whitehead Conjecture that every subcomplex of a finite aspherical 2-complex is aspherical, or is the knot-like case strictly weaker?

evidence.quote: whether this knot-like case of the Whitehead Conjecture is equivalent to, or strictly weaker than, the finite case of the Whitehead Conjecture
